title: Interactive Context Engineering Lab
disclaimer: This lab provides deterministic, source-grounded practice feedback. It does not make legal, compliance, security, financial, or other professional determinations, and it does not use external AI grading.

scenarios.title: Assemble a Grounded Subscription-Downgrade Context
scenarios.summary: Choose the smallest useful context package for a customer asking why a subscription was downgraded.
scenarios.scenario: A customer asks why their subscription was downgraded. The response must use the official downgrade policy, the customer’s current account facts, and a friendly tone without speculation.
scenarios.instructions: Select every component that belongs in the working context. Leave out material that does not help this bounded task.

options.label: Role: customer support agent
options.description: Defines the operating role for the response.

options.label: Rules: do not speculate; be concise; state when information is missing
options.description: Sets the no-invention and response boundaries.

options.label: Dynamic facts: account status, plan type, and current date
Grounding: the relevant downgrade rule and remediation options
options.description: Provides the approved evidence needed to explain the change.

options.label: Task: explain this customer’s downgrade and provide next steps
options.description: Keeps the job bounded to the immediate request.

options.label: Output: explanation, next steps, and missing information needed
options.description: Makes the answer scannable and reviewable.

options.label: Memory: the customer’s entire historical chat archive
options.description: This broad history is not required for the bounded task and may add noise.

options.label: Tool: unrestricted public web search
options.description: The task should be grounded in approved policy and account facts, not open web content.

options.label: Example: an unrelated refund email
options.description: An unrelated example consumes context without improving this answer.

rubric.label: The package is bounded to the downgrade question.
rubric.support: Chapter 1 asks for a role, constraints, dynamic facts, policy excerpts, and a structured output.

rubric.label: Approved policy and account facts ground the answer.
rubric.support: The source scenario requires official policy plus current account status.

rubric.label: The rules prevent speculation and expose missing information.
rubric.support: The source scenario explicitly requires no speculation and a missing-information path.

rubric.label: The output contract contains explanation, next steps, and needed information.
rubric.support: The source scenario specifies these three output elements.

scenarios.title: Improve a Weak Incident-Summary Context Envelope
scenarios.summary: Replace a vague incident prompt with a legible operating package another person can review and run.
scenarios.scenario: An operations analyst currently pastes raw incident notes and says, “Be helpful and summarize this.” The workflow needs confirmed facts, open questions, current incident data, explicit no-invention rules, a bounded task, and a fixed status-update structure.
scenarios.instructions: Complete the labeled context-envelope fields. The application checks structural coverage only; it does not judge the professional correctness of your wording.

fields.label: ROLE
fields.prompt: Who is the model acting as?

fields.label: RULES
fields.placeholder: Include no invention and assumption labeling.

fields.label: REFERENCE / CONFIRMED FACTS
fields.placeholder: Describe where confirmed notes and evidence belong.

fields.label: MEMORY / OPEN QUESTIONS
fields.prompt: Record continuity that matters for this incident.
fields.placeholder: Separate confirmed facts from unresolved questions.

fields.label: DYNAMIC FACTS
fields.placeholder: Incident ID, severity, start time, current impact, last updated.

fields.label: TASK
fields.placeholder: Create a status-ready incident summary from approved notes.

fields.label: OUTPUT
fields.placeholder: Timeline / Current Impact / Hypotheses / Next Actions / Owner Requests

fields.label: CHECKS / MISSING-EVIDENCE BEHAVIOR
fields.prompt: State review checks and what happens when evidence is missing.
fields.placeholder: Do not fill gaps; label uncertainty; ask for missing facts.

selfChecks.label: Rules, evidence, dynamic facts, task, and output are visibly separated.
The package says not to invent facts and to label assumptions or uncertainty.
The package defines what to do when evidence is missing.
Another person could understand and run the package without hidden explanation.

rubric.label: All seven context-envelope sections plus checks are populated.
rubric.support: Chapter 3 Lab 3 specifies ROLE, RULES, REFERENCE, DYNAMIC FACTS, TASK, OUTPUT, and CHECKS; the source incident scenario also uses memory.

rubric.label: The package separates instructions, evidence, current state, and output expectations.
rubric.support: Shaping quality depends on explicit labels and logical ordering.

rubric.label: Missing evidence leads to uncertainty or a request for information, not invention.
rubric.support: The Chapter 3 lab explicitly requires missing-evidence behavior.

rubric.label: The context envelope is understandable by another person.
rubric.support: The source deliverable is a reusable envelope another person can run without extra explanation.

provenance.locator: Practice labs; Lab 3 — Shape a reliable context envelope
provenance.support: Required envelope sections, explicit output contract, and missing-evidence rule.

scenarios.title: Diagnose an Unsupported Proposal Guarantee
scenarios.summary: Trace a confident but unsupported proposal claim to its failure pattern and smallest credible mitigation.
scenarios.scenario: A proposal draft says the company “guarantees zero disruption.” The approved source describes a transition objective but does not authorize a guarantee.
scenarios.instructions: Choose the failure pattern, likely cause, smallest credible mitigation, and regression check supported by the source playbook.

choices.label: The workflow converted an objective or past outcome into an unapproved guarantee.
The tone was not enthusiastic enough.
Add an evidence-only rule: goals, approaches, and past outcomes may not become guarantees; create an Evidence Gap when support is insufficient.
Paste the full proposal library into every context.
Increase creativity so the claim sounds more persuasive.
Remove the test case that exposed the problem.
Re-run the same requirement with the same source and confirm that no guarantee appears without explicit evidence.
Test only an unrelated marketing question.
Accept the next answer if it looks polished.
Remove the source and ask the model to rely on memory.

rubric.label: The issue is classified as an unsupported claim rather than a generic quality problem.
rubric.support: Chapter 4 requires failure-mode diagnosis before selecting a fix.

rubric.label: The cause is tied to the evidence boundary.
rubric.support: The source playbook identifies conversion of objectives into guarantees as the diagnosed failure.

rubric.label: The mitigation is narrow and evidence-based.
rubric.support: Use the smallest credible change that prevents unsupported guarantees and exposes evidence gaps.

rubric.label: The same case is re-run to protect the corrected behavior.
rubric.support: Chapter 4 requires re-testing on the same evaluation set and preserving regression cases.

provenance.support: Unsupported “guarantees zero disruption” claim, diagnosed cause, evidence-only mitigation, and regression case.

scenarios.title: Compare Two Support-Assistant Governance Designs
scenarios.summary: Choose the safer and more useful design for unauthorized account requests and prohibited exceptions.
scenarios.scenario: A customer support assistant uses an internal knowledge base. Customers may request account details they are not authorized to see or exceptions support is not allowed to grant.
scenarios.instructions: Compare the two designs, choose the stronger one, and identify the source-supported reasons for the choice.

designs.label: Design A — broad helpfulness
designs.text: Answer every customer request helpfully. Use any available account data. If the customer insists, try to find an exception. Keep refusals brief so they do not frustrate the customer.

designs.label: Design B — governed assistance
designs.text: Verify authorization before using account details. Apply approved policy and refusal rules. For prohibited requests, explain the boundary clearly, preserve a professional brand tone, provide an allowed next step, and route ambiguous or exception cases to human review. Use a pre-call authorization check and a post-call boundary/output check.

reasons.label: It makes authorization and policy precedence explicit.
It refuses clearly while giving an allowed next step.
It uses professional tone without weakening the boundary.
It places moderation and review checks in the workflow.
It exposes more account data to maximize helpfulness.
It avoids human review so every case is automated.

rubric.label: The decision hierarchy is explicit.
rubric.support: Chapter 5 says a strong answer makes the decision hierarchy explicit.

rubric.label: The refusal is clear, professional, and action-oriented.
rubric.support: The source scenario requires helpful refusal behavior rather than vague or accusatory language.

rubric.label: Brand tone supports trust without weakening the boundary.
rubric.support: Tone applies to both normal answers and refusals.

rubric.label: Pre-call and post-call checks are concrete workflow steps.
rubric.support: The source scenario treats moderation as a workflow design, not a generic safety statement.

provenance.locator: Practice scenario 2: Policy and refusal behavior for a support assistant
provenance.support: Authorization boundary, refusal behavior, brand tone, and pre/post checks.

provenance.locator: Security: prompt injection and data exfiltration; least privilege
provenance.support: Trusted instruction separation and access limited to the sources and actions required for purpose.

scenarios.title: Build a Safe Update Plan for a Finance Assistant
scenarios.summary: Create a structured release and monitoring context for a proposed finance-assistant prompt update.
scenarios.scenario: A finance operations assistant summarizes approved reimbursement policy and routes edge cases for review. Users say the assistant is too rigid, and the team wants to update the prompt without weakening policy, escalation, or reliability.
scenarios.instructions: Build the operational context below. The application checks that the source-required decision areas are present; professional reviewers must still judge whether the plan is correct for a real organization.

fields.label: PURPOSE AND BOUNDED CHANGE
fields.prompt: What behavior is being changed, and what must remain protected?
fields.placeholder: State the narrow usability problem and protected policy/escalation behavior.

fields.label: VERSIONED ASSETS
fields.prompt: Which production assets must be named and versioned?
fields.placeholder: Prompt, policy block, retrieval rules, rubric, escalation criteria.

fields.label: METRICS
fields.prompt: Which quality, risk, and user-experience signals will be monitored?

fields.label: REGRESSION SET
fields.prompt: Which routine and edge cases must be re-tested?
fields.placeholder: Include normal policy questions, missing information, exception pressure, and escalation cases.

fields.label: STAGED ROLLOUT
fields.prompt: How will the candidate be introduced gradually?
fields.placeholder: Define stage, audience, review window, and evidence required to expand.

fields.label: ROLLBACK AND FAIL-SAFE TRIGGERS
fields.prompt: What signals stop or reverse the release?
fields.placeholder: Name thresholds, unsafe behavior, policy weakening, or operational failure.

fields.label: REVIEWERS AND OWNERS
fields.prompt: Who reviews the update and why?
fields.placeholder: Include finance, compliance, operations, and the named workflow owner where appropriate.

fields.label: SAFE FALLBACK
fields.prompt: What happens when the preferred path is unsafe, unclear, or unavailable?
fields.placeholder: Route to human review, provide approved policy only, ask for missing information, or pause action.

selfChecks.label: The plan balances quality, risk, and user experience.
The regression set includes routine and edge cases.
Rollout and rollback criteria are part of the release design.
The plan names the perspectives required for review.
A clear fallback exists for unsafe, unclear, or unavailable conditions.

rubric.label: The proposed change is bounded and protected behavior is named.
rubric.support: Enterprise release discipline begins with identifiable, versioned components and intended behavior.

rubric.label: Metrics and regression cases support a go/no-go decision.
rubric.support: The source scenario asks for metrics plus routine and edge regression cases.

rubric.label: Staged rollout and rollback triggers are explicit.
rubric.support: The source scenario treats rollout and rollback as part of the release design.

rubric.label: Named reviewers and owners cover finance, compliance, and operations perspectives.
rubric.support: The source says these perspectives matter to the final decision.

rubric.label: The plan defines fail-safe behavior.
rubric.support: Chapter 5 requires defined behavior when inputs, policies, tools, or conditions prevent safe normal operation.

provenance.locator: Practice scenario 3: Monitoring and safe updates for a finance assistant
provenance.support: Metrics, regression cases, staged rollout, rollback signals, and cross-functional review.

provenance.locator: Governed release; monitoring; fail-safes and graceful degradation
provenance.support: Versioned assets, monitoring, rollback, ownership, and defined fallback behavior.
